method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Magistrates Court (Civil Proceedings) Act 2004 (WA) (No. 48 of 2004), compilation as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_48918.txt (legislation.wa.gov.au mrdoc 48918, retrieved 2026-09-07); limits as in force on and after 1 January 2009 ($10 000 minor cases, $75 000 general); no regulations or rules of court used (not deposited): prescribed proceedings and the time for an appeal from a registrar are inputs or not encoded
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted statutory text is reproduced under CC BY 4.0 with the attribution in ../../SOURCE-LICENSE.md

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: ss 3, 4 (the $10 000 and $75 000 limits), 6(1), (5) (general civil jurisdiction and excluded claims), 7 (consumer, trader, consumer/trader claim), 10(2), 25(2), (5) and 31 (costs; allowable costs only at or under the minor limit), 26 (minor case), 27, 28 (minor cases or general procedure), 29, 45(1) (private, informal, rules of evidence), 30, 44 (lawyers and other agents), 32, 40(1), (3) (appeals and the 21 days). Out: ss 8, 9, 11-24 (save 16(1)(j), noted), Parts 5, 6, ss 41-43, 46-49, and pre-2009 limits.
lives: chloe c070 (2032-05-20): a new laptop fails in month three; the retailer repairs it -- if it had not, a minor case for a consumer/trader claim
